best_for: Windows users and admins who already have, or plan to run, a WireGuard server or peer and need the official client to bring tunnels up on their PC.
description:
WireGuard is an open source VPN tunnel created by Jason A. Donenfeld and published by ZX2C4 and Edge Security. The project keeps its code small on purpose, so that one person can read and audit all of it, and the protocol is set out in a published academic whitepaper.

The tunnel shows up as an ordinary network interface on your computer, which you manage with the usual network tools. Each peer is tied to the tunnel addresses it is allowed to use, and packets from anyone else are dropped. Traffic travels over UDP, and a connection follows you when your IP address changes, for example when your laptop moves from home Wi-Fi to a phone hotspot. For help, the project runs an IRC channel on Libera.Chat and a mailing list.

points.title: A client, not a VPN service
points.text: WireGuard is a protocol and a tunnel program. It comes with no servers; you need a server or peer config, either your own or one from a VPN provider that supports WireGuard.

points.title: Small and quick to set up
points.text: Each side holds a private key and knows the other's public key, much like SSH keys. The project aims for setup as simple as SSH, using modern cryptography such as Curve25519 and ChaCha20.

points.title: The official Windows route
points.text: The project calls this client, built on its WireGuardNT driver, the only official and recommended way to run WireGuard on Windows. The installer picks the right build for your CPU and checks its signature.

points.title: MSIs for deployment
points.text: Standalone MSI packages for x86, x64 and Arm64 install for all users and suit admins pushing it to many machines. Registry keys change how the app behaves for managed setups.

points.title: Windows 10 and newer
points.text: The Windows client supports Windows 10 and 11 and Windows Server 2016 to 2025. The Windows listing keeps 28 versions.

points.title: Mac and Linux get it elsewhere
points.text: This site lists only Windows. On a Mac the app comes from the Mac App Store; on Linux, WireGuard is part of the kernel and the tools come from your distribution.
